# Schema

Reference for `storage/loom/index.json`. The authority is `schema/loom-index.schema.json`; the tables below are generated from it, descriptions included. For reading an index from PHP, see the [PHP API](php-api.md).

Every top-level field is required, empty arrays are valid, `null` is never valid for an array, and unknown top-level keys are rejected. A trailing `?` on a field name marks it optional. Fields marked "Filled by the cross-link pass" start empty in each scanner and are joined afterwards.

## `events[]`

Event classes.

| Field | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | string | Canonical identifier; the FQCN for class events. |
| `fqcn` | string | Fully qualified class name. |
| `kind` | one of `class` | Only `class` today. |
| `file` | path | File declaring the class. |
| `line` | integer ≥ 1 | 1-indexed declaration line. |
| `dispatched_from` | array of [dispatchSite](#dispatchsite) | Dispatch sites that fire this event. Filled by the cross-link pass. |
| `handled_by` | array of object | Listeners that handle this event, one entry per listener and method, sorted by `listener`, `method`. Filled by the cross-link pass from `listeners[].handles`; closure listeners are not included. |

`events[].handled_by[]`

| Field | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `listener` | string | Listener FQCN. |
| `method` | string | Handler method on the listener. |

## `model_events[]`

Synthetic Eloquent model events from observer hooks and `Event::listen('eloquent.*')` strings. Emitted directly by the observer scanner; the cross-link pass does not regenerate them.

| Field | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | string | `eloquent.{event}: {model FQCN}`. |
| `kind` | one of `model_event` | Always `model_event`. |
| `model` | string | FQCN of the model. |
| `event` | one of `retrieved`, `creating`, `created`, `updating`, `updated`, `saving`, `saved`, `deleting`, `deleted`, `restoring`, `restored`, `replicating`, `trashed`, `forceDeleting`, `forceDeleted`, `booting`, `booted` | Eloquent hook name. `booting` and `booted` come only from `Event::listen('eloquent.booted: ...')` strings; observer methods match the other values. |
| `handled_by` | array of object | Observers and `Event::listen` targets, sorted by handler and method, deduplicated. The shape differs from `events[].handled_by` because observers are not listeners. |

`model_events[].handled_by[]`

| Field | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `handler` | string | FQCN of the observer or `Event::listen` target. |
| `method` | string | Observer hook or listener method. |
| `file` | path | Observer class file, or the file holding the `Event::listen` call. |
| `line` | integer ≥ 1 | Observer class line, or the `Event::listen` call line. |

## `listeners[]`

Listener classes. Handler methods include inherited ones.

| Field | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `fqcn` | string | Fully qualified class name. |
| `file` | path |  |
| `line` | integer ≥ 1 |  |
| `handles` | array of object | Events this listener handles, deduplicated by `event`, `method` and sorted by `event`, then `method`. |
| `registration` | one of `listen_array`, `auto_discovered`, `event_listen_call`, `subscriber` | How the listener was found: `subscriber` (a subscriber's `subscribe()` method, return-array or imperative form), `listen_array` (`$listen` in an `EventServiceProvider`), `event_listen_call` (`Event::listen()` in a provider), `auto_discovered` (typed `handle()` parameter). When several paths find the same listener the order is `subscriber`, `listen_array`, `event_listen_call`, `auto_discovered`. |
| `queued` | boolean | `true` when the class implements `ShouldQueue` directly or through a parent class or interface. A trait cannot confer it. |
| `dispatches` | array of [dispatch](#dispatch) | Events and jobs dispatched from the listener's handler methods. Filled by the cross-link pass. |

`listeners[].handles[]`

| Field | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `event` | string | FQCN of the event class. |
| `method` | string | Handler method. `handle` when the registration names none (auto-discovery, a bare `Listener::class`); a `[Listener::class, 'foo']` tuple keeps its method. |

## `observers[]`

Observer classes. One observer registered against N models gives N entries; when a pair is found through both paths, `attribute` wins over `observe_call`.

| Field | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `fqcn` | string |  |
| `file` | path |  |
| `line` | integer ≥ 1 |  |
| `observes` | string | FQCN of the observed model. |
| `registration` | one of `observe_call`, `attribute` | `observe_call` for `Model::observe(Observer::class)`, including `static::observe()` in `booted()`; `attribute` for `#[ObservedBy]`. |
| `hooks` | array of one of `retrieved`, `creating`, `created`, `updating`, `updated`, `saving`, `saved`, `deleting`, `deleted`, `restoring`, `restored`, `replicating`, `trashed`, `forceDeleting`, `forceDeleted` | Observable model events the observer has a method for, sorted. |
| `dispatches` | array of [dispatch](#dispatch) | Dispatches made from the observer's hook methods. Filled by the cross-link pass. |

## `unresolved_dispatches[]`

Dispatch sites whose target could not be resolved statically. Never dropped silently.

| Field | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `file` | path |  |
| `line` | integer ≥ 1 |  |
| `expression` | string | Pretty-printed source of the unresolvable expression. |
| `reason` | one of `dynamic_class_name`, `container_resolution`, `string_concatenation`, `conditional_dispatch` | `dynamic_class_name`: `event($variable)` and similar. `container_resolution`: class fetched from the container (`app()`, `resolve()`, `->make()`). `string_concatenation`: name built by concatenation or interpolation. `conditional_dispatch`: a ternary or conditional whose branches cannot be evaluated. |

## `closure_listeners[]`

Closure and arrow-function listener registrations. They have no class name, so each site is one entry and none is joined into `events[].handled_by`. Not deduplicated. Dispatch sites inside `[line, end_line]` of the same file belong to it, including sites in nested closures.

| Field | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `event` | string | FQCN for `::class` registrations, the raw string for string-keyed ones. |
| `file` | path | File holding the closure, not the registration call. |
| `line` | integer ≥ 1 | 1-indexed first line of the closure. |
| `end_line` | integer ≥ 1 | 1-indexed last line of the closure; equals `line` for a one-line closure. |
| `registration` | one of `listen_array`, `event_listen_call`, `subscriber` | `listen_array` (closure in `$listen`), `event_listen_call` (second argument of `Event::listen()`), `subscriber` (inside a subscriber's `subscribe()`, as a return-array value or an imperative `$events->listen()`). |
| `queued` | boolean | Always `false`; closure queue detection is not done. |
| `dispatches` | array of [dispatch](#dispatch) | Dispatches attributed to the closure by source span. Filled by the cross-link pass. |

## `scheduled_tasks[]`

Task scheduler entries, one per chain. Deduplicated on `file`, `line`, `kind`, `target`; kernel and bootstrap forms win over the facade form. A `job` target can be joined to `jobs[].fqcn` client-side; there is no back-pointer.

| Field | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `kind` | one of `command`, `job`, `closure`, `exec` | Decided by the root call. `command`: `->command()`, target is the signature string verbatim or the FQCN for a `::class` argument. `job`: `->job()`, target is the FQCN. `closure`: `->call()`, target is `null` for an inline closure and `Class::method` for a tuple or `Class@method` callable. `exec`: `->exec()`, target is the shell command. |
| `name` | string or null | The `->name()` label verbatim, or `null`. |
| `target` | string or null | Depends on `kind`; `null` for an inline closure. |
| `arguments` | array of string | `command` kind only, else `[]`. The literal parameters of `->command(Class::class, [...])`: plain items as the stringified value, keyed items as `key=value`, booleans as `true`/`false`; unresolvable items are skipped. |
| `queue` | string or null | `job` kind only: the second argument of `->job($job, $queue)`. |
| `connection` | string or null | `job` kind only: the third argument of `->job($job, $queue, $connection)`. |
| `cron` | string or null | Canonical five-field expression for every recognised frequency helper (`daily` is `0 0 * * *`; `cron()` is passed through verbatim). `null` when no recognised helper appears, its argument is a variable, or the last helper is unrecognised. The last frequency helper in a chain wins, as at runtime. |
| `frequency` | object or null | Sub-minute interval for `everySecond` and its six siblings, whose cron is `null`. `null` for every other entry. At most one of `cron` and `frequency` is set; the last helper wins. |
| `timezone` | string or null | From `->timezone()`. |
| `without_overlapping` | boolean | `->withoutOverlapping()` appears in the chain. |
| `without_overlapping_expires_at` | integer or null | Expiry minutes from `->withoutOverlapping($minutes)`. `null` without a literal argument; the framework default of 1440 is not invented. |
| `on_one_server` | boolean | `->onOneServer()` appears in the chain. |
| `run_in_background` | boolean | `->runInBackground()` appears in the chain. |
| `even_in_maintenance_mode` | boolean | `->evenInMaintenanceMode()` appears in the chain. |
| `constraints` | array of string | Opaque labels for non-cron restrictions, sorted ascending: day of week (`weekdays`, `sundays`), time window (`between(8:00,17:00)`), conditions (`when(closure)`, `skip(closure)`), environments (`environments(production,staging)`). They sit beside `cron`, not inside it. |
| `file` | path | File of the root call (`->command`, `->job`, `->call`, `->exec`). |
| `line` | integer ≥ 1 | Line of the root call, not the trailing modifier. |

`scheduled_tasks[].frequency`

| Field | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `unit` | one of `seconds` | Only `seconds` today. |
| `every` | integer ≥ 1 | Interval length in `unit`. |

## `routes[]`

HTTP routes, one per route. A route registered against several verbs is reported as `ANY`.

| Field | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `method` | one of `GET`, `POST`, `PUT`, `PATCH`, `DELETE`, `OPTIONS`, `HEAD`, `ANY` | HTTP verb, uppercase. |
| `uri` | string | Route URI with enclosing group prefixes applied; always starts with `/`, the root is `/`. |
| `name` | string or null | Group name prefix concatenated as-is with the route's own `->name()`; `null` when unnamed. |
| `controller_fqcn` | string or null | `null` for closure and non-controller routes. |
| `controller_method` | string or null | `null` for closure and non-controller routes. |
| `middleware` | array of string | Names as written, including those inherited from enclosing groups. Aliases and groups are not expanded. Source order. |
| `file` | path | File of the route definition. |
| `line` | integer ≥ 1 | 1-indexed line of the route definition. |
| `end_line`? | integer ≥ 1 | Last line of a closure action. Present only for closure actions. |
| `dispatches` | array of [dispatch](#dispatch) | Dispatches from the controller method, or for a closure route those within `[line, end_line]` of the file (each such event lists the route in `dispatched_from`). Filled by the cross-link pass; empty when the controller cannot be resolved. |

Notification classes.

| Field | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |

## Shared shapes

Referenced from several sections above.

### `relativePath`

Path relative to the app root, forward-slashed. Never absolute: a leading `/`, `\` or drive letter is rejected.

### `queueConfig`

Queue properties read from class property literals. A key is `null` when the class declares no such property (the framework default applies at runtime). The literal keeps its own type.

| Field | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `connection` | string or integer or null |  |
| `queue` | string or integer or null |  |
| `delay` | string or integer or null |  |
| `tries` | string or integer or null |  |
| `timeout` | string or integer or null |  |
| `backoff` | string or integer or null |  |

### `dispatchSite`

One place where a class is dispatched, sent or notified from. Shared by every `dispatched_from`, `sent_from` and `notified_from` list.

| Field | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `file` | path |  |
| `line` | integer ≥ 1 |  |
| `method` | string | Origin of the dispatch: `Class::method` for code in a class method (a pass-through closure such as `DB::transaction(fn () => ...)` counts for the enclosing method), `VERB /uri` for a route closure, `Class::$dispatchesEvents[hook]` for a model's `$dispatchesEvents` entry. |
| `mode`? | one of `sync`, `after_response`, `push` | How the call form executes, omitted for plain forms whose outcome follows the target's `queued` flag. `sync`: `dispatchSync`, `dispatch_sync`, `dispatchNow`, `sendNow`, `notifyNow`. `after_response`: `dispatchAfterResponse`, `->afterResponse()` on a chain. `push`: `Queue::push/pushOn/later/laterOn/bulk`, `Mail::queue/onQueue/queueOn/later/laterOn`. The `ShouldQueue` flag and the `sync` driver are not evaluated. |
| `overrides`? | [dispatchOverrides](#dispatchoverrides) | Dispatch-time modifiers found at the call site. Omitted when none. |
| `channels`? | array of string | Notification-only. The literal channel filter of `Notification::send($users, $n, $channels)` or `sendNow(...)`, which overrides the notification's `via()`. Lowercased names or channel-class FQCNs. Omitted when absent, empty or non-literal. |

### `dispatchOverrides`

Fluent modifiers resolved statically at the call site. Only keys that were found are present, and the object is omitted when none were. A non-literal argument leaves its key absent.

| Field | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `locale`? | string | From `->locale('es')`. |
| `mailer`? | string | From `->mailer('ses')`. |
| `connection`? | string | From `->onConnection('redis')`. |
| `queue`? | string | From `->onQueue('high')`. |
| `delay`? | integer ≥ 0 | From `->delay(60)`, integer seconds only; `now()->addMinutes(5)` and variables leave it absent. |
| `after_commit`? | boolean | From `->afterCommit()`; only ever `true`. |

### `dispatch`

A resolved dispatch made from a class method or closure.

| Field | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `target` | string | FQCN of the dispatched event or job. |
| `kind` | one of `event`, `job` | Whether the target is an event or a job. |
| `confidence` | one of `high`, `medium`, `low` | Always `high` for statically resolved targets; `medium` and `low` are reserved. |
| `file` | path |  |
| `line` | integer ≥ 1 |  |

## Determinism

Two scans of identical source produce byte-identical JSON, except `scanned_at`. Files are read in sorted path order, and every section is sorted by its natural key followed by tie-breakers, so the order is total:

| Section | Order |
|---|---|
| `events`, `model_events` | `id` |
| `listeners`, `jobs`, `mailables`, `notifications` | `fqcn` |
| `observers` | `fqcn`, `observes` |
| `closure_listeners` | `event`, `file`, `line`, `end_line`, `registration` |
| `scheduled_tasks` | `file`, `line`, `kind`, `target`, `name`, `cron` |
| `routes` | `file`, `line`, `method`, `uri`, `name` |
| `unresolved_dispatches` | `file`, `line`, `expression`, `reason` |

Nested sets use the same rule: dispatch sites by `file`, `line`, `method`, `mode`; `dispatches[]` by `file`, `line`, `target`, `kind`; `handled_by[]` by `listener` (or `handler`), `method`; `handles[]` by `event`, `method`. Arrays whose source order is meaningful (`middleware`, `channels`, `arguments`) keep it. Paths are relative to the app root, so scanning the same tree from another directory gives the same output.

## Versioning and breaking changes

Two versions, two jobs:

- `schema_version` (`"MAJOR.MINOR"`) is the version of the document shape. **Consumers key on this.** The schema pins the major (`^1\.[0-9]+$`).
- `loom_version` is the version of the package that wrote the file. It is informational; nothing should branch on it.

Rules for `schema_version`:

| Change | Bump |
| --- | --- |
| New optional field, new enum value, new section | Minor |
| Required field made optional | Minor |
| New **required** field | Major |
| Optional field made required | Major |
| Field renamed, retyped or removed; enum value removed; section removed | Major |
| Bug fix that doesn't change shape | None |

Reader behaviour, in `IndexLoader`, `loom:check` and `loom:diff`:

- Same major, any minor: loads. Unknown keys are ignored.
- Missing `schema_version` (written before 1.0), older major or newer major: refused with a message to re-run `php artisan loom:scan`. There is no migration; the index is a derived file.
- `loom:diff` refuses to compare two indexes with different majors, and exits `2`.

`schema_version` `1.0` is the baseline and is frozen: every field name, enum value and nullability on this page, and the MCP tool names and inputs in [MCP tools](mcp-tools.md), follow the table above from here. Before it, `loom_version` was the only marker and several shapes changed without a bump (for example `closure_listeners[].end_line` and `scheduled_tasks[].name` became required). Those changes are folded into `1.0`; from here the table above applies strictly.

Because the schema sets `additionalProperties: false`, a consumer that validates with a stored copy of the schema will reject a later minor. Validate with the schema shipped in the same release as the producer, or don't validate.

## Open enums

Some enums grow in minor releases. Consumers must tolerate values they don't know and must not fail on them:

- `kind` on dispatch entries (`event`, `job` today)
- `registration` on listeners and observers
- `reason` on `unresolved_dispatches[]`
- `confidence`: only `high` is emitted today; `medium` and `low` are reserved, ordered `high > medium > low`
- `routes[].method`
- `model_events[].event` and `observers[].hooks[]`, which follow Eloquent's event list
- `scheduled_tasks[].kind` and `scheduled_tasks[].frequency.unit`

Removing or renaming a value is a major change. Adding one is minor.

What to do about it:

- Pin the Loom version you build tooling against, and upgrade deliberately.
- Read the [changelog](https://github.com/lucasp1337/laravel-loom/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md) before upgrading; shape changes are listed there.
- Regenerate the index with `php artisan loom:scan` after every upgrade instead of reusing an old file.
